results.summary_before: This analog block generates a temperature-stable reference voltage of about 1.2 V using a pseudo-PTAT current generator with enable-gated startup. It is used by applying a 1.8 V supply and asserting the appropriate enable pins (ui[6] and ui[3]) to obtain the reference on ua[0]. Testing requires a voltmeter to measure the output and verify low temperature dependence. The design is notable for including a startup circuit that can be toggled if the bandgap fails to start.

results.summary_before: This SystemVerilog design implements an AXI4-Lite slave with a read-only ID register and 32 general-purpose registers, providing a 16-bit readback path on the bidirectional pins. It is used by driving the address, write/read requests, and data through the input and bidirectional pins, with read data appearing on the outputs. No external hardware is required for basic operation, though a host controller is needed to exercise the AXI4-Lite interface. The design serves as a demonstration of integrating a standard bus protocol into a Tiny Tapeout project.

results.summary_before: This SystemVerilog design translates Morse code entered via a push button into characters A-Z and displays the most recent two characters on seven-segment displays through a Digilent Pmod SSD. Timing rules distinguish dits (1 s hold), dahs (3 s hold), letter ends (3 s release), and word ends (7 s release), with an external LED blinking at 1 Hz to help the user keep time. It requires a tactile switch, an LED, and the Pmod SSD, and includes testbenches for the counting and translation modules. The project is a straightforward educational Morse decoder with no silicon test results reported.

results.summary_before: This project is a 4-channel PWM controller with SPI configuration, designed for half-bridge motor and LED driving. It includes configurable frequency, per-channel duty cycle and phase offset, dead-time insertion to prevent shoot-through, and fault protection that latches off outputs when the nFAULT input is asserted. The design requires an external SPI master and optionally a gate driver IC and power stage for motor control. It is notable for its comprehensive feature set and fault handling in a compact implementation.

results.notes: Removed alu: the design performs arithmetic rendering but does not implement an ALU.
results.summary_before: This project generates real-time VGA graphics using purely arithmetic logic, with no framebuffer or ROM. It cycles through four rendering modes (rings, plasma, interference, chaos) based on a frame counter, and every pixel is computed on-the-fly. The design requires a VGA monitor and a 25 MHz clock, and it automatically starts rendering and cycling through modes upon reset release. It is notable for its fully procedural approach and continuous animation.

results.summary_before: This is an 8-bit MIPS-inspired single-cycle processor with eight registers, an ALU, branches and jumps, scaled to fit one Tiny Tapeout tile. It runs a hardcoded program automatically after reset; three input pins select which register is shown on the eight outputs, while five bidirectional pins expose the program counter and one shows a halt flag. Testing needs only LEDs on the outputs and switches on the register-select inputs, with no external hardware required. It is notable for preserving core MIPS concepts in a very small area, though the documentation does not report silicon results.
